facts: On 2 August 1990 Iraq's army invaded Kuwait and took it in two days. President George H. W. Bush said the invasion would not stand. American troops poured into Saudi Arabia to defend it. On 17 January 1991 coalition air strikes began; Iraq fired Scud missiles at Saudi Arabia and Israel and Patriot batteries shot back. Six weeks later Kuwait was free. Retreating Iraqi troops set Kuwait's oil wells on fire, and it took months to put them out.

lines.say: On August 2nd, 1990, Iraq's army invaded Kuwait, and took it in two days.
President George H. W. Bush declared the invasion would not stand.
American troops poured into Saudi Arabia to defend the kingdom and its oil.
When coalition air strikes began, Iraq fired Scud missiles, and Patriot batteries shot back.
Six weeks later, Kuwait was free. Retreating troops left its oil wells burning for months.
